{{nihongo|'''Hakunu Shrine'''|波久奴神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ōmi Province]].

'''Hakunu Shrine''' (はくぬじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in Takahata-chō, {{ill|Nagahama, Shiga|Q844130|qid=Q844130}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|Q131358|qid=Q131358}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and its {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=former shrine rank}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}.

=== Enshrined deity ===
With {{ill|Takamimusubi|de|Takamimusubi|es|Takami-musubi-no-kami|fa|تاکامیموسوبی|fr|Takamimusubi|id|Takamimusubi|ja|タカミムスヒ|ks|تاکامِمُسُبی|pl|Takamimusubi|ru|Такамимусуби-но ками|zh|高皇產靈尊|qid=Q125400|lt=Takamimusubi}} as the principal deity, it also enshrines {{ill|Mononobe no Moriya|Q2424736|qid=Q2424736|lt=Mononobe no Moriya Ōmuraji}}.

=== Shrine crest ===
* Umebachi

=== History ===
Details of the founding of the principal deity are unknown. According to shrine tradition for the associated deity Mononobe no Moriya Ōmuraji, after losing to {{ill|Soga no Umako|Q1191233|qid=Q1191233}} in {{ill|587|Q30891|qid=Q30891}} (Yōmei 2), he fled with Urushibe Kosaka to this area, his own territory. To evade pursuit by the {{ill|Soga clan|Q909854|qid=Q909854}}, he hid in a cave in the eastern gorge of Kotani-yama in October of that same year, then built a grass hut in a place thick with {{ill|Hagi|Q413694|qid=Q413694}} in Takahata, took the name Hagio no Okina, and instructed local people. After his death, villagers built a {{ill|Hokora|Q1442984|qid=Q1442984}} in memory of his virtue and revered him as "Senior First Rank Hagino Daimyōjin."

In {{ill|1881|Q7808|qid=Q7808}} (Meiji 14), it was ranked gōsha; in Meiji 34, Mononobe no Moriya Ōmuraji was {{ill|Co-Enshrinement|ja|合祀|qid=Q11412524|lt=enshrined together}} and shrine buildings were organized; in Meiji 41 it received designation as a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shinsen Heihaku-ryō Kyōshinsha}}.
